name: feral-special-fatalite-2-attempt-01a
prompt:
Create an ORIGINAL native RGBA sprite sheet as a new drawing of Feral Predator, NOT a rig or mirror. LANDSCAPE composition 1536 wide by 1024 high. EXACTLY TWO COLUMNS and FOUR ROWS, eight separate full-figure cells, each cell 768x256. All figures on this page face RIGHT, front/right three-quarter view. The other facing will be independently drawn on another page. VERY SMALL FIGURES: standing body from mask crown to feet about 150 pixels and NEVER taller than 180 pixels; this deliberately leaves transparent space. With mannequin, both standing bodies must use that same150px body height, combined scene width under550px. A full transparent gutter at least40px must surround EVERY scene. Do not use all available cell height. No figure, hand, spear tip, foot or prop may enter neighboring cells. Native alpha: every pixel outside each separate scene exactly alpha0. NO cast shadow, NO ground plane, NO glow, NO gradient, NO smoke, NO text, NO visible grid. Opaque well-lit detailed body, but illumination NEVER painted into empty transparent pixels.
Identity matches inspected references exactly: lean sinewy ochre spotted skin, black dreadlocks, ivory bone skull mask with exposed red mandibles, dark segmented loincloth, asymmetrical bone ornaments, bronze bracers, ankle wraps/clawed feet; no shoulder cannon. Gear anatomically consistent: shield on LEFT forearm, right wrist bracer as source. Complete Feral body choreography study with a neutral jointed adult-sized gray training mannequin, NOT an actual victim/combat sprite. Feral holds TWO spear halves, one per hand, with no whole third spear. A simple training blade belongs only to the mannequin. Left shield folded, wrist blades retracted; no gore.
Read cells left to right then top to bottom, not a comic panel. Cell1 is body-scale calibration ONLY: Feral alone in neutral full-body guard with two spear halves held lowered, no mannequin in the calibration row. Cell1 is outside animation; no mannequin or spare props in calibration. Seven completely new independently articulated source choreography stages occupy cells2 through8:
Cell2: The mannequin presents its short training blade; Feral deflects it outward using the first spear half in his RIGHT hand, contact and weight transfer clear.
Cell3: Feral steps close to the mannequin while maintaining the right-hand parry; left spear half draws back for the second action.
Cell4: He delivers a short LEFT-hand spear-half thrust against the mannequin's armored torso in silhouette, no wound or blood, right weapon keeps its parry line.
Cell5: Feral withdraws the LEFT half while the gray mannequin slumps and drops its simple training blade, neither Feral weapon disappears.
Cell6: Feral looks down to verify the slumped mannequin is no longer advancing; his own two weapons remain controlled and lowered, no victory salute.
Cell7: He aligns and rejoins the two halves into one compact spear and begins stowing it, left shield folded, mannequin still slumped, no anatomical trophy.
Cell8: Feral secures the rejoined compact spear at his real hip holder, both hands releasing only once it is held; the gray mannequin and dropped training blade remain slumped nearby.
Every mannequin is an obviously gray articulated training dummy, no human face, blood, gore, injuries, trophy or terror. Whole body effort, contact, controlled withdrawal and recovery must be distinct. This is a SCENE CHOREOGRAPHY VISUAL STUDY; synchronization with a separate actual opponent is not claimed. Keep exact same props through the sequence. Do not leave duplicate weapons where Feral already collected them. Do not replace a finishing sequence with seven victory poses. Draw all cells newly, not repeated neutral silhouettes.
DIRECTION IS MANDATORY: every mask nose points toward the RIGHT EDGE. Feral is on the LEFT HALF of every scene cell and the training mannequin on its RIGHT HALF. No mirrored art.
The entire scene is like a TINY MINIATURE in the CENTER HALF of each cell, not a body filling the frame. Leave at least a full quarter-cell blank above and below each scene, even crouches. Retract right wrist blades entirely inside the bracer in every drawing; no protruding silver tips at all.
